name: Eco-Panels of Tennessee, Inc.
old_description: Along with having the lowest utility bills of all your neighbors, you'll have the safest, strongest, and most advanced built home of them all with Eco-Panel SIPs. Beware the waste of common construction and live smarter, forever.
about:
Eco-Panels of Tennessee, Inc. operates from Red Boiling Springs in Clay County, Tennessee, with its 35,000-square-foot manufacturing plant in nearby Hermitage Springs. The company was established in 2012 as a licensed franchise location for Eco-Panels, LLC of Mocksville, North Carolina, expanding to meet rising demand for structural insulated panels. It belongs to a family-owned group of businesses that has produced systems-built housing products and forestry commodities since the late 1970s, making it the largest non-governmental employer in the area.

The facility manufactures high-performance structural insulated panels (SIPs) for residential and commercial building applications. Using state-of-the-art technology, the plant produces panels in a wide variety of sizes, shapes, and configurations, achieving industry-leading insulation values of R-26 in 4.5-inch panels and R-40 in 6.5-inch panels. The panels are described as two to three times stronger than conventional framing, with a foam core that contains no volatile organic compounds and does not melt at any temperature.

Eco-Panels serves homeowners, builders, and architects across the residential and commercial construction sectors, including timber-frame projects. Testimonials cite successful collaborations with individual homeowners such as Micah Mazanowski and Eric O’Donnell, as well as firms like 423 Dwell, LLC and licensed contractor Roger West. The company provides design assistance, installation guidance, and on-site training to support both professional crews and DIY builders.

The business was founded to offer a more economical, sustainable, and safer alternative to traditional construction. The company emphasizes lower utility, building, and labor costs with less waste, long-term energy savings, and reduced wood usage. As a franchise of the North Carolina–based Eco-Panels system, it leverages a proprietary panel technology marketed for its strength, environmental profile, and speed of assembly.
